body: A practical Indian stack is: Screener.in (screens + 10-yr financials + annual reports/concalls links) for discovery, then primary filings (BSE/NSE announcements, annual reports, credit-rating rationales, shareholding/pledge/SAST disclosures) for verification, with Trendlyne/Tijori/Tickertape/Chartink as supplements and Valuepickr for crowd-sourced deep dives. Screener queries are plain-English field names joined by AND/OR with comparison operators; public screens like "Coffee Can Investing" are good templates.

- No pledge flag on Screener.
- No dilution: equity capital flat at ₹6 cr.
- Debtor days are 32. FY26 CFO was 1.9x PAT.

**Named cause**
- Its grain-ethanol distilleries, built with debt in FY22-24, are now running at about 82% utilisation.
- Ethanol EBITDA margin was 16% in H1 FY27 against 8% a year earlier.
- The 2026-27 allocation is 1.97 lakh KL, worth about ₹1,305 cr.
- Q2 FY27 PAT was ₹39 cr, +151% (Multibagg, Arthneeti, Univest).

**Why not BUY-ZONE**
- The margin is a feedstock spread, not a franchise. Management says ethanol becomes unviable with maize above ₹26-27/kg. Maize is at ₹30-32/kg now, and H2 ethanol margins are guided 1-2 percentage points lower.
- Full-year ethanol EBITDA guidance is 11-12%. Q2 OPM has already dipped to 11%.
- Institutions are absent: DII went to zero and FII is only about 0.3%.
- The positives are real: deleveraging (397 to 234, with an HSBC loan exit targeted by February), 5.9x P/E and a reverse DCF implying only about 2% growth.

**Bull case**
- If FY27 sales are ₹2,600 cr at 10-11% EBITDA (guidance), PAT would be ₹140-160 cr. At 9-10x, market cap would be ₹1,400-1,600 cr, 1.4-1.6x.
- Grain-price normalisation plus a ₹100-120 cr sorbitol/maltodextrin capex could add a less cyclical leg.

**Kill criteria**
- OPM below 8% in Q3/Q4 FY27.
- Debt rising above ₹300 cr.
- The ethanol procurement price is not revised up while grain costs stay high.

body: **Summary:** Cement is a regional, heavy, low-value product that can travel only ~300–500 km by road. Profit is EBITDA per tonne: realisation minus energy (pet coke, coal and power, ~25–30% of cost), freight (~25–30%) and raw materials, times volumes. Pricing depends on regional supply discipline. Key metrics: EBITDA/tonne (~₹900–1,300 normal, ₹1,400+ peak), capacity utilisation (~65–75% industry), realisation per tonne, cost per tonne (power and fuel, freight, lead distance), volume growth against the industry, trade/premium share, net debt/EBITDA, capex per tonne (~$80–120/t greenfield) and market share. Cycle drivers: housing, infrastructure and rural demand; supply additions (consolidation: UltraTech plus Adani now hold ~50%+ capacity), fuel prices, the monsoon (Jul–Sep weakest quarter) and pre-election construction. Lead indicators: the cement index in the eight-core-industries data (monthly), dealer price checks (brokers' monthly channel checks), pet coke prices, state capex, and the Ministry of Commerce/DPIIT production index. Winners (Shree Cement on cost leadership, UltraTech on scale and acquisitions, Dalmia in the East) had the lowest-quartile cost and lead distance, captive power and green energy, and disciplined capacity addition in their regions. Losers were high-cost single-plant players and over-leveraged acquirers (Jaiprakash Associates). Valuation: EV/EBITDA 12–20x or EV per tonne of capacity ($100–200/t; replacement cost ~$80–120/t). Nov 2026: UltraTech's Q2 FY27 EBITDA/tonne was ₹974, down ~20% QoQ on fuel cost but up ₹60 YoY, with volumes +13.8% and utilisation 71%. Prices rose 7–10%/bag in late September and ~5% further in October. Traps: capacity wars and paying replacement-cost multiples at peak margins. Sources: [1](https://www.adityabirla.com/media/press-releases/ultratech-delivers-strong-q2-fy27-performance-net-sales-up-189-pat-up-213-domestic-volumes-up-138/) · [2](https://www.spglobal.com/energy/en/news-research/latest-news/metals/102126-indias-ultratech-cements-domestic-volumes-rise-138-in-q2-despite-monsoon-disruptions) · [3](https://upstox.com/news/market-news/stocks/ultra-tech-acc-ambuja-risks-and-tailwinds-shaping-cement-stocks-after-q1-fy-27/article-198794/) · [4](https://news24online.com/business/ambuja-strengthens-trade-and-premium-mix-in-q2-amid-seasonal-external-headwinds/948149/)
